title: Experts disagree on rule_gate_budget_ms
context:
Chief architect: Not a real disagreement: both claims are compatible and both are adopted. Measuring the 6000 ms budget from the start of the pre-edit hook is what makes the issue's promise ('the host timeout then never fires') hold, since about 1 s of fixed gate work sits before the scripts; the tiny-budget, injected-clock test from the qa seat is how it is proven. Pick this option to accept the pair.

Target: rule_gate_budget_ms
- performance-analyst: the 6000 ms budget is measured from the start of the capability-gate-pre-mutation hook, not from the start of the rule scripts, so the fixed gate work (about 1.0 s measured) plus the scripts stays under the 10 s host timeout
- qa-engineer: Given strict mode and a deterministic changed-files script slower than a tiny budget (e.g. 50 ms), when an Edit hits the pre-mutation seam, then the edit is allowed with the exact additionalContext text and a pending-pre-mutation marker is written; when the turn ends and that script fails, the completion seam blocks; when it passes, the marker is cleared. Tests use an injected clock or tiny budget, never real 6 s waits.
